timing.label: Objection 2 (technical)
timing.question: Why do the two dashboards show different totals?

problem.quote: Two people were blocked this morning by two different caps

approach.quote: I will fix each one with the cap that actually blocked it

evidence.quote: Trailhead has used its full 3,000 ACU, from Enterprise Consumption for this billing window

next_step.quote: Ask: approve those numbers as this month's team caps

must_mention.point: Organization limit and per-user tier are enforced independently; either one blocks, and raising one never lifts the other
must_mention.evidence_quote: Devin enforces both independently, and either one stops new work. Raising one never lifts the other

must_mention.point: The Trailhead lead is at 180 of 400 on her tier but Trailhead is at 3,000 of 3,000, so only an enterprise admin raising the org limit helps
must_mention.evidence_quote: Trailhead is at 3,000 of its 3,000 limit, so only an enterprise admin raising the organization limit helps her

must_mention.point: The per-user meter counts cloud plus local usage and leaves Devin Review out; the org limit includes Review
must_mention.evidence_quote: 250 cloud plus 160 local. His 90 ACU of Devin Review are not in it

must_mention.point: Limits reset on the contract day, the 23rd, after the 18–20 Nov sale, and temporary overrides expire then
must_mention.evidence_quote: the limits reset on the contract day, the 23rd, which is three days after the sale ends

must_mention.point: Newest vs Legacy is the gear-icon Version setting; Cloud-only metrics exclude local usage; the empty state means no billing cycle in range
must_mention.evidence_quote: a Cloud-only number on the Newest version of analytics, picked with the gear icon next to the date picker, so it leaves out local usage

must_mention.point: A tier applies to each member, not a pooled team budget; a team cap is an organization-level limit
must_mention.evidence_quote: A tier applies to each member separately; it is never a pooled team budget

must_mention.point: The finance update carried exactly three ACU figures, each with the view it came from
must_mention.evidence_quote: used its full 3,000 ACU, from Enterprise Consumption … adds 900 ACU, from the merchandising lead's sale plan … raises Trailhead to 4,200 ACU

article_plural_slips: "we review them actually on the 23rd" — drop "actually"; "we review them on the 23rd"

accuracy.anchor: Seven of seven points with their numbers; the per-user vs org split carried by 180/400 against 3,000/3,000 (anchor: 27–30 = all points, correct mechanism).

structure.anchor: Outcome → Evidence → Risk → Next action → Ask held, each heading spoken (anchor: 22–25 = order held throughout).

customer_relevance.anchor: Led with "both people can work again today"; every figure named its view (anchor: 18–20 = customer outcome first, sourced numbers).

brevity_and_fluency.anchor: All six segments within ±5 s; one filler, no tag questions, no long pauses (anchor: 12–15 = on target, under 1 filler/min).

recovery.anchor: Both objections acknowledged, bounded, evidenced and closed with an offer (anchor: 9–10 = pattern held twice).

stems: "Two caps, two jobs: the organization limit is the team budget, the tier is the per-person guardrail." — keep it as your opening line.
"This number includes local usage; that one does not." — say it before the second number in every comparison.
"We review them on the 23rd." — the same close without the filler.
previous_run_comparison: First recorded run for dryrun on lab 11; no previous run to compare with.
